policy.note: During the Phase 27 freeze, product-code changes require an auditable blocker entry tied to the pull request. Empty is the expected steady state.

blockers.justification: Phase 33 corrects cross-surface identity continuity, preserves existing Nvet roles during CTG One linking, hardens signed Android releases to the canonical production API, and removes legacy mobile branding before Play distribution. These protected product changes address release-blocking account divergence and mobile release consistency defects without authorizing commercial launch.

Phase 34 closes the release-blocking Android identity gap by adding CTG One authorization-code plus PKCE federation, encrypted native verifier/state handling, reliable cold-start callbacks, canonical Nvet session persistence, and exact preservation of Nvet role authority including SUPERADMIN. It also converges the web/mobile visual source of truth without authorizing commercial launch or weakening the frozen payment and external-evidence gates.

Phase 35 hardens the Android artifact that will be evaluated by Google Play: release cleartext transport is denied while emulator-only HTTP remains isolated to debug, R8/minification becomes a tested release invariant, and CTG One federation is incorporated into the Play Data Safety and automated compliance contracts. The phase preserves draft-only Play automation, manual production promotion, operator-owned signing/console evidence, and the independent payment-provider gate.

Phase 36 adds privacy-minimized mobile runtime and CTG One federation observability, release-health SLO evaluation, and explicit integration with the existing append-only beta evidence boundary. These protected changes are required to detect operational regressions before real beta activation while keeping Play Vitals, physical-device evidence, real user cohorts and elapsed observation windows operator-owned and fail-closed.

Phase 37 closes release-blocking dashboard authority and role-convergence defects: ADMIN/SUPERADMIN mobile sessions must not fall through CLIENT navigation, SUPERADMIN must inherit ADMIN capabilities consistently beyond RolesGuard, and the canonical beta control plane must expose the Phase 36 observation-evidence boundary. The phase adds regression certification without authorizing commercial launch, mutating production data, or weakening external payment and operator evidence gates.

Phase 39 remediates the critical/high production dependency findings surfaced by Phase 38, starting with the vulnerable bcrypt/node-pre-gyp/tar installation chain and compatible transitive refreshes. Dependency and lockfile mutations are intentionally isolated behind this audited release-blocker PR, with full backend/mobile/Android/RC regression gates and no authorization of commercial launch, Play publication, provider configuration changes or production database mutation.

Phase 44 closed the process-restart durability gap for idempotent appointment creation and introduced the local recovery record required for a safe financial continuation. Its post-merge P1 review identified that the continuation still needed to be connected to explicit user-confirmed payment resumption, which is tracked by Phase 45 rather than reopening background financial replay.

Phase 45 closes the P1 continuation gap discovered after Phase 44: a booking recovered after process restart now persists an explicit financial handoff and exposes user-confirmed payment resumption from appointment detail. Payments remain excluded from background replay, the original idempotency contract is reused, stale handoffs are discarded when backend transaction state advances, and no provider configuration or commercial launch boundary is changed.

Phase 46 closes a cross-platform release-readiness defect in which persisted React Query and Zustand state was not explicitly owned by one authenticated Nvet user. The phase makes logout/account switching a hard state boundary on web and mobile, purges legacy/unowned caches, disconnects mobile chat and payment-recovery handoffs, and tightens mobile backend reconciliation without adding product functionality or authorizing financial background replay, provider mutation, Play publication or commercial launch.

Fixes a release-blocking regression introduced by Phase 46: adoptSessionCacheOwner/clearSessionCache called queryClient.clear() from inside the login/register/logout mutation's own mutationFn, wiping the mutation cache mid-flight and orphaning that mutation's observer so its onSuccess (and the post-login navigation transition) never fired. This is the confirmed cause of the Android Detox E2E failure that was on main. The fix scopes the cache purge to queryClient.getQueryCache().clear(), additionally purges every non-'auth' mutation from the live MutationCache at the session boundary (closing a cross-account paused-mutation leak found in review), and adds regression tests for both. Merged; authorizes no commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication.

Closes a second, distinct root cause of the same Android Detox E2E failure left open after PR #258/#259 merged: queryClient.getQueryCache().clear() (the #258 fix) still detaches any QueryObserver already mounted on a query key, and RootNavigator's useCurrentUserQuery() is mounted on 'auth','me' at the exact moment adoptSessionCacheOwner runs inside the login mutation's mutationFn, so the subsequent setQueryData never reaches the mounted component. Verified empirically against the real @tanstack/react-query library with a new integration test. Replaces the query-cache clear with queryClient.removeQueries({predicate: ...}) scoped to non-'auth' queries, which never touches the auth observer's own query. A post-merge P1 review also found that clearSessionCache() is called directly (not through a cache-clearing mutation) by authService.logoutAllDevices(), changePassword() and deleteAccount(); since qk.auth.me() has staleTime: Infinity, clearSessionCache() now writes null through that same preserved observer so those flows end the session immediately instead of leaving the previous user visibly authenticated. Merged; authorizes no commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication.

Closes 9 of the 19 production high-severity dependency findings tracked as temporary exceptions in docs/production/PHASE_38_VULNERABILITY_EXCEPTIONS.json (expiring 2026-09-21T15:56:00Z, fail-closed): brace-expansion, browserslist, engine.io, form-data, nanoid, shell-quote, socket.io-adapter, socket.io-parser, ws. Each is pinned via root package.json overrides to a confirmed-patched non-major version; none are imported directly by application code. The remaining 10 findings require semver-major NestJS (10->12) and React Native (0.75->0.87) migrations and are deliberately left as open, separately tracked exceptions rather than attempted inside this frozen RC. Regenerates package-lock.json (npm install --legacy-peer-deps, matching CI) and reformats 6 unrelated backend files via eslint --fix as an incidental, no-logic-change consequence of a transitive prettier patch bump pulled in by the regeneration. A P1 review finding that the brace-expansion override forced an unrelated, already-safe major line (minimatch@10.2.6's brace-expansion@^5.0.8..^5.0.12) down to the older 2.1.7 was fixed by scoping that one dependent out of the blanket override and pinning it to ^5.0.9 (the first patched release in its own line) instead. Merged; authorizes no commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication.

Corrects release-blocking veterinary marketplace inconsistencies across pricing, commissions, memberships, booking amount authority and legacy database convergence. The change preserves veterinarian price autonomy, removes simulated plan activation, centralizes commercial policy, and adds an auditable paid-plan pending state without authorizing commercial launch or weakening payment, security, backup or operator-evidence gates. Merged into main as PR #265; the blocker is retained as resolved audit history.

Introduces the pilot-phase manual TRANSFER payment flow requested for the first month of user/vet acquisition, before a PSE gateway is formalized for CTG One Technology S.A.S.: the CLIENT now pays the company's own Bre-B account directly and submits the proof (FinancialOperationsService.submitTransferProof authorizes the client, not the vet, which now receives 403), a new public GET /payments/transfer-destination exposes the env-var-configurable pilot account, and admin confirm/reject actions now post automatic SYSTEM chat notices on the appointment thread. Reuses the existing TRANSFER state machine, private/magic-bytes-validated storage, and admin transfer-tracking review queue without modification. Updates the payment-rail-certification workflow and script to certify the vet is explicitly forbidden from submitting proof before certifying the client path. No commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication is authorized; the vet's net payout continues through the existing VetWithdrawal mechanism, unchanged by this PR. Merged into main as PR #264; the blocker is retained as resolved audit history.

Closes a functionality gap surfaced by the pet/vet/chat feature audit: pet creation had no way to attach a photo despite Pet.photo and the mobile pickImage() helper already existing unused. Adds POST/DELETE /pets/:id/photo, ownership-checked via the existing requireOwner guard and uploaded through the shared StorageService (magic-bytes validated, public visibility, image-only allow-list) behind a dedicated PetsModule Multer config mirroring the vets/payments upload modules. Mobile MyPetsScreen gains a camera/gallery photo picker in the create/edit modal and renders the uploaded photo on the pet card. No changes to money, settlement, entitlement, KYC, wallet or identity paths; authorizes no commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication. Merged into main as PR #266; the blocker is retained as resolved audit history.

Adds the exact manual-transfer QR asset used by the client transfer flow in mobile chat so the pilot company-account payment destination can be rendered from repository-owned source bytes without network transformation. This is an asset-only protected product change and does not alter settlement logic, provider configuration, payment authorization, commercial-launch status, or Play publication boundaries.

Post-merge follow-up to PR #266, closing two bugs a Codex review surfaced after merge. First, StorageService's local driver (the default without Cloudinary) returned a relative /uploads/public/... URL that main.ts never mounted as static content, so pet photos — the first public upload in this codebase to use the local driver, since every other caller's folder is forced-private — were unreachable; fixed by mounting the local public upload directory in main.ts and having uploadToLocal return an absolute URL via a new PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL env var. Second, MyPetsScreen's Save button only tracked the create/update mutation's pending state, re-enabling before the awaited photo upload finished and allowing a double-tap to create a duplicate pet; fixed with a dedicated isSaving state covering the whole operation. No changes to money, settlement, entitlement, KYC, wallet or identity paths; authorizes no commercial launch, provider mutation, or Play publication.
